market_context.summary: Term-premium regime, and one rotation session that colours every finding below. FRED has the 10-year at 5.19% (2026-10-14) against a 3.88% fed funds effective rate, the 2-year at 4.82%, and the 10y-2y spread flattening to +0.33. September CPIAUCSL rose 0.65% m/m - an ~8% annualized run rate - while UNRATE ticked up to 4.2% from 4.1%. A long end above 5% driven by term premium and inflation rather than growth is a headwind to long-duration equity and to rate-sensitive sectors. The 2026-10-15 session was NOT a broad rally: SPY +0.28% and QQQ -0.13% against IWM +1.37%, XLV +1.86%, XLF +1.38%, SLV +3.39%, NKE +5.21%, LULU +5.31%, EFX +7.25% - a single-session rotation out of AI/tech into beaten-down laggards, with XLE -1.58% as the source of funds. Every capitulation reversal and 50-day reclaim in this report is that same one day seen through a different ticker, and none has a second day of confirmation.

data_quality_notes:
Research ran 06:02-06:37 ET inside the pre-open window and closed with a RESEARCH COMPLETE block, so nothing here is reconstructed from a cut-off and `truncated` is false. Eleven distinct candidates were captured; eight are published and three are on the watchlist.

THE ONE CAVEAT THAT MATTERS MOST: 2026-10-15 was a single rotation session out of AI/tech into beaten-down laggards (IWM +1.37%, XLV +1.86%, XLF +1.38%, SLV +3.39% against QQQ -0.13%). CVS's 50-day reclaim, ABT's volume day, KMX's gap-up, DKS's base high and the NKE and LULU rallies the two shorts are being held through are ALL that same one day seen through different tickers. They are one observation, not six, and none has a second day of confirmation. Size accordingly.

WHAT SYNTHESIS RECOMPUTED. Every reward-to-risk ratio and stop distance below was recalculated from the final entry, target and stop against ATR14 fetched this morning, not carried from the research notes. All eight published ideas clear their floors: ratios 2.06-2.42 against the 2.0 swing floor, stops 2.06-3.60 ATR from entry against the 2.0 stock-swing floor. Claimed win probabilities run 2.6 to 12.8 points above the 1/(1+R:R) break-even, so nothing claims an implausibly large edge.

RATIO CLUSTERING, STATED PLAINLY. Four ratios sit between 2.06 and 2.17, which is the signature of targets fitted to clear a floor, so here is what actually happened. The targets were anchored independently - 120-day highs for ABT (117.34), CVS (110.68) and KMX (65.28), and for DKS a base-width projection (164.97) that a 14.3x multiple on the company's own guidance midpoint reaches a second time. What was fitted is the ENTRY BAND, not the target: on ABT, CVS, KMX and DKS both band edges were derived from the two constraints, so the band is the window where the published target and the published stop both pass. KMX's band is only 40 cents wide for that reason. That is the floors binding the entry rather than the target being walked up to meet them, but it does mean these trades have no geometric margin for being roughly right about the entry - a fill outside the band is a different trade. GE (2.06) and LULU (2.07) are restatements of positions published weeks ago and were not fitted today at all.

POSITION UPDATES, NOT NEW RISK. Five of the eight rows are updates to open positions and carry their original filled entries restated for the record: GE (hold into Monday's pre-open print), NKE and LULU (hold both shorts, each with a new falsifiable 50-day cover rule), SMMT (hold, 1% lottery ticket). Their entry bands are NOT orders - every one says so in `entry.condition` - and judged at the `ideal`, the fill that actually happened, all of them pass both floors. Four rows are new ideas: DKS, ABT, CVS, KMX.

TWO POSITIONS CLOSED AND THE PRIOR-CONTEXT TABLE DOES NOT KNOW IT. MU and EEM both had their published stops breached intraday on 2026-10-15 and are on the watchlist as closure notices, not recommendations. MU traded 858.00 against an 870.00 stop (-9.4%) and then reversed 8.5% to close at the day's high; EEM traded 62.81 against a 63.00 stop (-4.0%) and closed back ABOVE its own stop at 63.96, so a reader checking the last price would wrongly see a live position. Neither is re-entered. SNX is the third watchlist demotion and the only judgement call in this report: it is a live position whose published 242.50 stop now sits 1.84 ATR from entry - inside the 2.0 floor - because ATR14 expanded to 9.4893 after publication. A filled position's stop cannot be widened to fix that, so rather than publish an idea that fails its own floor, synthesis demoted it with the reason stated. The stop stands; the position is unchanged.

CORRELATION. Healthcare carries two long rows (ABT medtech, CVS managed care) - under the cap of three, different sub-drivers, but they bounced on the same single session and must not be read as confirming each other. Consumer discretionary carries four rows but as two opposed pairs: long DKS and KMX (retailer value with insider clusters) against short NKE and LULU (brand earnings power). Two same-direction rows per side, under the cap, and the pairs partially hedge - all four rose together on 10-15.

COVERAGE GAPS, each attempted rather than skipped. No intraday idea: today's five dated catalysts are all before-the-open bank and insurer prints, and with no working pre-market quote source at 06:00 ET any intraday level would be a guess about a print not yet seen. No long_term idea: the lane needs a defended bear-case price clearing 2.5:1, and nothing got there - ELV has the best evidence screened but no fetchable guidance to value it from, and DKS at 10x the low end of guidance gives a 110 bear case and only 2.15:1 to the pre-crash 204.50, so clearing 2.5 would have meant stretching the multiple to 19x. It was published as the swing it actually is. No futures idea: no CME contract price was obtainable, and naming a contract month with levels not fetched would be fabrication - the rotation read would otherwise have pointed at long /M2K against short /MNQ. No crypto idea: spot returned (BTC 81,840, ETH 2,445.83, SOL 105.89) but history failed on every configured source, so there is no ATR and the 2.5 ATR crypto stop floor cannot be computed; a stop written without it would be a guess dressed as a risk control. No event-contract idea: Kalshi was reachable and returned zero markets on all eight topics tried, so no implied probability could be quoted against ours.

SOURCES THAT FAILED: Yahoo quotes and history (HTTP 429 on every index, macro and crypto symbol - so no index level, VIX, DXY, gold or WTI price appears anywhere in this report), Yahoo options (HTTP 401, so no options-implied move is cited on any idea), Finnhub CFD indices (subscription required), api.nasdaq.com short interest (ReadTimeout on every call - this costs the NKE and LULU shorts the most, since crowding is precisely the risk a rotation into laggards exposes and it is the one thing that could not be measured), Kalshi events (reachable, zero markets), Nasdaq history for BTC-USD, Stooq, TwelveData and AlphaVantage (no API key). SOURCES THAT WORKED: Finnhub quotes, history and ATR, earnings calendar, insider transactions, recommendation trend and surprises; FRED; CoinGecko spot; computed relative strength.

PRICES. Every `last_price` is the 2026-10-15 16:00 ET close, re-fetched by synthesis at 06:36 ET and matching the research figures exactly. The market was closed, so this is the freshest honest price available and not stale data. No price in this report is estimated.

THREE THINGS THE MECHANICAL VALIDATION RAISED, HANDLED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT FOR THE READER. (1) The research phase reported that DKS was on no earnings calendar through 2027-01-14. That was wrong. A re-fetch by synthesis puts DKS Q3 on 2026-11-23 at an EPS estimate of 1.417, and the catalyst field is corrected to say so. It does not change the trade - 26 sessions out is beyond this swing horizon, so the print is still not the driver and is still not counted as evidence - but a wrong calendar claim is exactly the kind of error that is worse than a missing one. (2) Validation reported ABT, CVS, KMX and GE as 'not on the fetched calendar'. They are: the calendar endpoint caps at 1,500 rows, so a wide window truncates. Synthesis re-verified each date in a narrow window - GE 2026-10-19 bmo (est 2.0576), ABT 2026-10-21 bmo (est 1.4302), CVS 2026-11-04 bmo (est 1.66), KMX 2026-12-16 (est 0.4724), SMMT 2026-11-11 (est -0.2928). Every date published below is confirmed. Where the calendar leaves the session blank - DKS, KMX, SMMT - no bmo/amc is asserted and the date is published without a time. (3) DKS failed the spread check at 17.75%, and that number is an artifact of the hour, not the instrument: the book was sampled at 04:01 ET at bid 122.19 / ask 145.99, on a name that traded 2.37M shares and carries $398M of average daily dollar volume. Books sampled closer to 06:30 ET read normally - ABT 0.31% at 06:26, CVS 1.62% at 06:36 - so the wide print is an empty pre-market book rather than a real cost of trading DKS. It is flagged here unresolved rather than waved away: the honest instruction is to check the live spread at the open before placing the 138.00-141.30 order, and not to trade it on a 17% book if that is really what the open shows.

TARGET REACH. Validation also notes that four targets sit beyond its 6.0 ATR guide for a 15-session swing - DKS 6.25, ABT 6.06, CVS 7.78, LULU 7.45. These are not fitted numbers (each is a period high, a base projection, or a level published weeks ago), but the warning is fair: all four need more than an ordinary swing's worth of range to reach, so the realistic outcome on them is a partial move rather than a tag, which is why DKS and CVS carry explicit scale plans.

TRACK RECORD CONTEXT. The book is 3 of 21 closed at target with an average of -5.3%, and conviction-3 ideas are 1 of 13. That sample is under the ~15-trade noise threshold per category, so it is not being over-fit, but it is the reason four of the eight rows here are sized at 2% and the single conviction-2 row at 1%.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). Two of eight cut, three conviction-4s cut to 3, two positions resized, one duplicated evidence item deleted, six ideas survive.

CUT, KMX (was rank 5). The only new idea in the report carrying a stop_distance warning, and the warning was load-bearing. 2.17:1 was produced by a stop 2.06 ATR from entry; re-cut to an honest 2.5 ATR the risk goes 5.20 to 6.31 and the ratio falls to 1.79:1, under the 2.0 floor. The idea never cleared the bar - the ratio was earned by the stop's placement, not by the target. The 40-cent entry band synthesis published as 'the one window where this trade is publishable' is the same finding stated from the other side. The positioning case was the best screened this morning and is preserved in full on the watchlist with a republish trigger.

CUT, GE (was rank 6). A live position demoted to the watchlist as an open position held on its published 292.00 stop - it is unchanged, it is simply no longer a recommendation. Its own thesis says 'the only new information is that Q3 lands Monday before the open,' which is a binary pre-open gap the stop cannot cover, not evidence of direction. Remove it and what remains is one technical level on a stock at 312.00 beneath a 331.65 SMA50. The row's own counter-argument calls it 'a stock in a downtrend being held because it was bought.' Its 2.06:1 was also the thinnest in the report and flattered by a 2.31 ATR stop: at 2.5 ATR it is 1.91:1. The entry cannot be re-cut, because it filled. This follows the SNX precedent set earlier in this same report.

WHY ONE KILL AND NOT FOUR. Four rows carried stop_distance warnings (NKE 2.08, KMX 2.06, GE 2.31, SMMT 2.36 ATR) and all four got the widened-stop test at 2.5 ATR. NKE holds at 2.02:1 and SMMT at 2.06:1, so their ratios are not artifacts. KMX and GE fail it. They are then treated differently on a stated rule: a NEW idea's stop is a choice made this morning, so a ratio that only clears the floor because the stop sits inside the cluster band is a fitted number and the idea dies - that is KMX. A FILLED position's stop is a price already live and cannot be re-cut to fix anything, so the test cannot kill the trade, only the claim made for it - GE comes off the recommendation list and the position stands.

NO IDEA SCORES ABOVE 3 TODAY, and that is a finding rather than the conviction-3 default this report has collapsed into before. Each of the three 4s lost it for a named defect in its third confirmation. ABT: `dated_catalyst` was the 10-21 pre-open print, an event the row's own key_risk lists as the thing that can open below the stop - counting a coin flip as support for a long is the double-count conviction exists to stop; of the two real legs, the insider buying is five months stale at 11-16% below the band. CVS: `dated_catalyst` is disclaimed inside its own catalyst field as 'not an earnings bet,' so it cannot also score the conviction, leaving an analyst book and a single 50-day reclaim the row itself calls the most common false signal there is. DKS: three real kinds, but the insider cluster is net +$81,802 against $5,588,664 gross and revisions improved by a figure the row calls trivial. In all three the live technical leg is the 2026-10-15 session - the one rotation day synthesis already flagged as five rows seeing one observation. The red team's reading is that the flag was right and the conviction scores had not been reduced to match it.

RESIZED. ABT 3% to 2% and CVS 3% to 2%. The correlation test applied to capital instead of to count: two healthcare longs is under the cap of three, but at 3% each they were the two largest positions in the report while resting on one shared observation, which sizes them as though they confirmed each other. The pair is now 4%. ABT has the independent reason too - DKS is held at 2% for a litigation date 13 sessions out, so 3% into a real pre-open print 3 sessions out was inconsistent with this report's own sizing.

EVIDENCE DELETED, NKE. The third item was filed as `counter_argument_answered` and contained no new fact: 'no company news per two independent write-ups' is the positioning item and 'stalled at the 37.643 50-day' is the technical item, the same confirmation entered twice under a second kind. Deleted; conviction stays 3 on the two genuine kinds that support it. NKE is otherwise the strongest row here - +0.44R expectancy, 0.32% spread, survives the stop test, and a cover rule checkable on a daily close - and moves from rank 4 to 3, ahead of CVS, which needs 7.78 ATR in 15 sessions off a first 50-day reclaim.

RISK ADDED THAT NEITHER ROW COULD SEE. NKE and LULU are one exposure, not two: both short beaten-down consumer brands, both lifted by the same 2026-10-15 rotation, both held on a 50-day cover rule, and the short-interest fetch failed on both - so the one measurement that would size the crowding is missing on each and a squeeze takes them together. 4% is short this theme, partially hedged by the DKS long, leaving the consumer book net short 2%. Both are kept, each having its own level and its own falsifiable rule, but if the two 50-days give way in the same week that is one signal, not two.

WHAT WAS NOT CUT AND WHY. DKS's spread FAIL at 17.75% is accepted as an artifact of a 04:01 ET book on a name carrying $398M of average daily dollar volume, which is synthesis's argument and it holds. But the enforcement pass re-samples the book rather than reading this note, so if it still reads a spread above 4% the demotion is CORRECT and must be allowed to stand - do not hand-edit the validation block to save the idea. The DKS target got a different fix instead: 164.97 is the base width projected from the 142.56 breakout level while the entry band tops out at 141.30 inside the base, so the measured move begins at a high DKS has not cleared - 10-15 printed 142.56 and closed 1.72 under it. The 14.3x anchor keeps the level defensible and the trim at 155 keeps it realistic; a tag is not the base case. SMMT is left exactly as published: at 1% with a stop 0.85 ATR below spot it is a position likely to be closed by noise, and its own row says so in those words, which is the disclosure doing its job rather than a defect to fix. LULU survives on review - the 'sources disagree on the exact catalyst' line in its positioning evidence reads as a weakness and is actually the thesis: a move nobody can attribute is a flow event. Validation demoted 1 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 5 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.

recommendations.thesis: Abbott is the laggard of a sector that worked: XLV is +20.86% over six months while ABT is +9.65%, leaving it -10.79% off its 117.34 high. The thing that makes this cheap rather than broken is that three officers bought it with their own money into the de-rating - Starks 10,000 shares at 92.65, Boudreau 2,200 at 91.50, Stratton 2,000 at 86.82, $1,301,477 across April-May 2026 - and the sell side has been moving the same way since, strong_buy 10 to 12 and bullish share 75.8% up 5.2 points over four months with zero sell ratings in any month.
recommendations.key_risk: ABT is the sector laggard and may simply deserve to be: six-month relative strength is -11.21% against XLV, so the trade needs the gap to close rather than widen, and nothing fetched proves it will. The 2026-10-21 pre-open print is a gap event outside market hours, so a miss can open below the 97.00 stop and the realized loss would exceed the stated 6.00 points. The entry also sits below the market, which per the house rules is the style whose fills select for the ideas already failing - accepted here only because the 100.862 20-day and the 97.20/97.39 low cluster are levels that exist.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is the one the research could not answer with evidence: ABT has lagged XLV on every window measured - 1 month -3.34%, 3 months -6.02%, 6 months -11.21% - and buying a persistent laggard because insiders did is a bet that they are early rather than wrong. The insiders bought at 86.82-92.65, which is 11-16% below the band, so a fill here is not the price they liked. RED TEAM. Conviction cut from 4 to 3 and size from 3% to 2%, for the same reason. The three evidence kinds that bought the 4 are not three confirmations of direction: `dated_catalyst` is the 10-21 pre-open print, which is a coin flip the row itself lists under key_risk as the thing that can open below the 97.00 stop - an event counted as support for a long is the double-count conviction is supposed to prevent. Of the two that remain, the insider buying is from 2026-04-23 to 05-07, five to six months stale, at 86.82-92.65, which is 11-16% below the band, and the technical leg is the 2026-10-15 rotation session. That leaves one live confirmation and one old one. The size cut follows from the same gap risk: DKS is held at 2% for a litigation DATE 13 sessions out, so ABT cannot carry 3% into an actual pre-open print 3 sessions out whose gap the stop does not cover. At 2% with ABT and CVS now 4% of capital between them, the healthcare pair is also no longer the largest exposure in a report where both legs bounced on one session.

recommendations.thesis: Update to the short opened 2026-09-08 at 38.40, now 37.14 and 3.3% in profit. Levels are unchanged and the reason is specific: the 5.2% rally on 2026-10-15 carried no company news. Coverage attributes it to investor rotation away from AI-related stocks lifting beaten-down consumer names, with XLY up 1% on a session SPY slipped, so it is a flow event rather than a change in the business. NKE remains down roughly 42% year to date and -33.3% off its 55.68 range high.
recommendations.key_risk: A rotation into laggards is exactly how a crowded short on a hated name unwinds, and this one has not finished: NKE closed 37.14 on 46.4M shares against a recent 19-30M, cleared its 35.38 20-day, and stopped 0.50 short of the 37.643 50-day. If that 50-day goes, the next buyers are the covering shorts and the 41.00 stop is only 3.09 ATR above the last close. Short equity also requires margin and the loss is unbounded above the stop on a gap. Short interest could not be fetched this morning, so the one measurement that would size the crowding risk is missing.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against holding is that a 5.2% day on 2.3x normal volume that clears the 20-day and closes at the 50-day is what the beginning of a trend change looks like, and no amount of calling it rotation makes that untrue. It is answered only by the level test now written into the action: the trade no longer relies on judging the rally, it relies on the 37.643 50-day holding, which is falsifiable on a daily close. RED TEAM. The third evidence item has been deleted rather than answered. It was filed as `counter_argument_answered` and introduced no fact of its own: 'no company news per two independent write-ups' is the positioning item, and 'the rally stalled at the 37.643 50-day' is the technical item. The same confirmation entered twice under a second `kind` is how a thin idea comes to look sturdy, and distinct kinds are the entire point of the count. Conviction stays at 3, which two genuine kinds support, but it now rests on two rather than on an apparent three. The position is otherwise the strongest thing in this report - best expectancy at +0.44R, 0.32% spread, a stop that survives being widened to 2.5 ATR at 2.02:1, and a cover rule that is checkable on a daily close - and it is held on that rule, not on the view that the rally was 'only' rotation.

RED TEAM. Conviction cut from 4 to 3 and size from 3% to 2%.
